verdicts.note: Self-identifies as 'a little girl'/female throughout; clear.
Mechanical confirmed by subject 'Yeah' to interviewer's question; cited quote is weak but variable holds (code 6 fits).
Enjoys work, 'don't get bored' = strong endorsement of interesting work.
Explicitly names 'challenging all the time' as the draw; strongly agree fits.
'never two days the same' directly supports variety appeal.
Narrow view (cars/aeroplanes) plus 'never really looked into it' supports chose with little knowledge.
'struggling for money', 'money would be handy' supports money motive at agree level.
Work experience repeatedly the key reason; strongly agree justified.
Frames 5 years experience as edge at interviews; supports improving job chances strongly.
'rose tinted glasses... seen things how it is' = seeing what industry/real world is really like.
Glad she works to be able to 'use this/make this' rather than only essays; thin but supports applying theory. Keep medium.
Two days uni, three days work = currently on placement; yes.
Actively sought placement; did NOT avoid it due to prior experience; strongly disagree defensible. Thin/inferential, medium ok.
Network 75 route confirmed throughout and by placement_status; code 2 fits.
'quite pleased that I did' = agree (4), not strongly; correct level.
Wanted more practical, 'only one subject' practical = level not just right; disagree fits.
Couldn't see relevance of management/communication modules; agree fits despite 'turned out alright' caveat. Medium ok.
Credits communication module with 'how to put things across to people'; supports course developing interpersonal skills.
Bus-with-40-boys quote describes male-dominated isolation and HER own confidence-building, not male students being more confident in class. Does not support construct.
Positive about group projects ('we've been quite good'); satisfaction reasonable. Medium ok.
Quote is about equal/fair treatment, not lecturer support per se; positive view of lecturers ('really good') gives weak support. Downgrade to low.
Positive about the one other girl, 'get on quite well'; supports satisfaction with friends made.
Names aerospace/own airline preference, not in list 1-10, so 'other' defensible (don't-know is an alternative given her uncertainty). Medium ok.
Quote 'see how I feel at the end' is general career uncertainty; never addresses further study. Coding 'no' from absence is unsupported.
Wanting to move to Australia/work for Qantas indicates travel/relocation matters, but offhand aspiration ('perhaps', 'not sure'); downgrade to low.
Quote is about industry trend (companies showing equal-opps to attract women), not whether equal-opp policies matter to HER job choice. Does not support the personal job-factor construct.
